name: Diameter
definition: The **diameter** $D(\mathcal{H})$ of a family $\mathcal{H}$ is the largest distance between two elements of the family, i.e. $$ D(\mathcal{H}):= \max_{h_1,h_2\in\mathcal{H}} |h_1\Delta h_2| $$
comments: The diameter is equal to the strict diameter dimension.
graph_summary: The greatest Hamming distance between two concepts in the class.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: Every pair of concepts in a subfamily remains a pair in the containing class.

p_monotonic.proof: Deleting coordinates cannot increase Hamming distance between two concepts.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Counterexample to strict c-monotonicity: for $\mathcal H=\{000,011,101,110\}$, split on the first coordinate.  Each fibre is a pair at diameter 2, while the full class also has diameter 2 (all distinct pairs have distance 2).  Thus the full value does not strictly exceed the smaller fibre value.
